title: Claude Code & the evolution of agentic coding — Boris Cherny, Anthropic
talk_summary: Boris Cherny argues Claude Code stays intentionally simple because models and UX are changing fast, then shares practical agent workflows: plan before coding, test-first iteration, tool onboarding via --help/memory, and parallel worktrees. The transferable mechanisms are workflow gates and context/memory practices, not product marketing.

takeaways.what_they_do: Tell the agent to write tests first, explicitly say they will not pass yet, commit the tests, then implement and commit code so it has a verifiable target to iterate against.
takeaways.evidence_quote: write the test first, commit, and then write the code and then commit.

takeaways.what_they_do: Have the agent explore the repo, produce a plan, and wait for approval before editing code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: have quad code explore and make a plan and run it by me before it writes code.

takeaways.what_they_do: Use tools to pull relevant files/logs into context first, then enable extended thinking; thinking before context is treated as wasted tokens.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If it's thinking up front, you're probably just kind of wasting tokens

takeaways.what_they_do: Run a CLI's --help, have the agent summarize usage into CLAUDE.md, and avoid building a custom bridge or extension unless advanced features are needed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: here's the CLI tool cla run-help. Take what you learn and then put it in the cloud MD.

takeaways.technique: Hierarchical memory and reusable command files
takeaways.what_they_do: Use root, subfolder, and home memory files loaded on demand, plus markdown command files exposed as reusable slash workflows.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You can also put in subfolders. Those will get pulled in on demand.

takeaways.what_they_do: Run multiple agents in separate git worktrees or CI actions; when coordination is unnecessary, have them write results to a markdown file.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you don't want to coordinate, the best way is just ask them to write to a markdown file.
